title: Prussian blue and Prussian white thin-film electrodes: single-step electrodeposition for anode and cathode applications
content: This study examines how deposition potential influences the composition and nanoscale structure of Prussian Blue (PB)/Prussian White (PW)-family films, providing an experimental basis for assessing their proposed functions. Films were grown directly on Au/Cr/Si in a single potentiostatic step from a common aqueous bath at −0.20 to +0.40 V versus a saturated calomel electrode, with a fixed deposition charge of 10 mC. Electron microscopy, elemental analysis, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy revealed potential-dependent chemistry and nonmonotonic morphology. EDS indicated greater K incorporation in lower-potential deposits, whose Fe 2p and Raman features were consistent with more reduced, PW-like environments. Surface K/Fe ratios varied nonmonotonically from 1.129 to 1.322 across the series, corresponding to 52.95–56.94% K within the detected K + Fe population. Larger faceted crystallites at +0.30 V contrasted with finer pyramids and cracks at +0.40 V. Selected PB-like and PW-like regions had local cubic lattice parameters of (10.31 ± 0.10) Å and (10.36 ± 0.10) Å, respectively; their overlapping uncertainties prevent discrimination by lattice spacing alone. Cross-sectional maps showed broadly uniform framework-element distributions within locally continuous coatings. Together, these observations relate deposition conditions to contrasting chemical and morphological starting states without establishing bulk stoichiometry or phase purity.
